standard.meaning: This wave records an assisted editorial, accessibility, and source-alignment pass for six inline instructional diagram placements.
standard.releaseBoundary: Independent review by a qualified subject-matter expert and production validation remain pending.

sourceDetails.title: What do we mean by Normal data?
sourceDetails.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sourceDetails.whyReputable: NIST’s Engineering Statistics Handbook gives the normal density, identifies mean and standard deviation as its parameters, defines the standard-normal transformation, and reports the 68.27, 95.45, and 99.73 percent areas.

sourceDetails.title: Ethical Principles of Psychologists and Code of Conduct
sourceDetails.whyReputable: APA publishes and maintains the governing code. Its current Ethics Office page identifies the 2002 code, amended in 2010 and 2017, while the code distinguishes five aspirational General Principles from enforceable Ethical Standards.

sourceDetails.title: Policy Statement on Evidence-Based Practice in Psychology
sourceDetails.whyReputable: APA’s official policy defines evidence-based practice in psychology as integrating best available research with clinical expertise in the context of patient characteristics, culture, and preferences, and emphasizes collaboration and ongoing monitoring.

items.title: Classic Language Labels Sit Within Distributed Networks
items.correctionSummary: Replaced one-to-one production and comprehension labels with historically anchored, anatomically qualified cards and a visible distributed-network model while retaining classic aphasia exam cues.

sourceDetails.title: Broca and Wernicke are dead, or moving past the classic model of language neurobiology
sourceDetails.organization: Brain and Language; PubMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine
sourceDetails.whyReputable: This peer-reviewed review evaluates the historical language model and explains why contemporary language neurobiology requires more precise anatomy, distributed cortical regions, subcortical contributions, and multiple white-matter pathways.

sourceDetails.title: The language network as a natural kind within the broader landscape of the human brain
sourceDetails.organization: Nature Reviews Neuroscience; PubMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine
sourceDetails.whyReputable: This recent peer-reviewed review characterizes a strongly interconnected, predominantly left-hemisphere frontal-temporal language network and supports teaching network-level organization rather than isolated one-function centers.

items.title: Dopamine Pathways Show Associations, Not One-Chemical Diagnoses
items.correctionSummary: Added a full alternative and learner title, raised every label to at least 12 units, replaced deterministic pathway claims with associations, and distinguished D2 antagonism from partial agonism and other drug-specific properties.
items.reviewNote: Diagram wording, labels, and placement were reviewed for source alignment, factual clarity, accessibility, and learner interpretation. Added a full alternative and learner title, raised every label to at least 12 units, replaced deterministic pathway claims with associations, and distinguished D2 antagonism from partial agonism and other drug-specific properties. sourceDetails.title: Dopamine receptor signaling and current and future antipsychotic drugs
sourceDetails.organization: Handbook of Experimental Pharmacology; PubMed Central, U.S. National Library of Medicine
sourceDetails.whyReputable: This peer-reviewed pharmacology review explains dopamine pathways, D1- and D2-family signaling, antipsychotic mechanisms, motor effects, Parkinson disease associations, and the important distinction between antagonism and functionally selective partial agonism.

sourceDetails.title: Canonical and Non-Canonical Antipsychotics’ Dopamine-Related Mechanisms
sourceDetails.organization: International Journal of Molecular Sciences; PubMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine
sourceDetails.whyReputable: This peer-reviewed systematic review summarizes contemporary dopamine-receptor mechanisms across antipsychotic agents while documenting variation in affinity, partial agonism, receptor profiles, treatment response, and adverse effects.

sourceDetails.title: Structural family therapy
sourceDetails.organization: American Psychological Association Dictionary of Psychology
sourceDetails.whyReputable: The APA Dictionary supplies a concise professional definition of structural family therapy that names subsystems, boundaries, hierarchies, coalitions, and enactment without reducing the model to a single boundary continuum.

sourceDetails.title: Families and Family Therapy
sourceDetails.organization: Harvard University Press; Google Books bibliographic record
sourceDetails.whyReputable: This is the bibliographic record for Salvador Minuchin’s foundational 1974 exposition. It documents the model’s attention to family organization, subsystem boundaries, adaptation, mapping, and restructuring.
